root.name: Latvian Gambit Accepted: Leonhardt Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Qf6 4. Nc4 fxe4 5. Nc3

overview: After 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.Nc4 fxe4 Black has regained the pawn and White plays 5.Nc3 hitting e4. Black must defend with ...d5 or ...Qg6 while the queen stays exposed. White is solid and slightly better while Black hopes for tricks.

white_ideas.idea: Hit e4 and trade queenside pieces

black_ideas.idea: Use the f-file and queen for counterplay

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with the e-file open
Black queen on f6 exposed to knight moves

character.notes: Early queen sorties and forcing tactics.

gambit.notes: Material is level at this point: each side has lost a pawn.

soundness.notes: Strong players think White is better.

structure.notes: Open lines, with the f- and e-files active.

approach.notes: Latvian lines are seldom seen from strong players.

level.notes: Specific tricks matter and it is dubious.

sublines_that_differ.name: Main 4.Nc4 fxe4 5.d3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Qf6 4. Nc4 fxe4 5. d3

character.reason: Early queen and an exposed king.

gambit.reason: The e4 pawn has been traded for e5, so material is level.

structure.reason: The centre pawns have been exchanged.

plans.reason: Black's queen is out early on f6.
